title: Staged egress migration runbook v0.2
content:
Goal:
Staged migration of on-prem/VPC egress for private deployments to the new proxy/NAT topology with minimal customer impact. This doc is a tactical runbook for the cutover and validation phases that bridges terraform module changes, firewall adjustments, and private DNS behavior.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: customer clusters in private deployments that currently use per-cluster NAT + split-horizon DNS. Target is to move to a centralized egress proxy cluster (kube-egress-proxy) fronted by a set of L4 VIPs, with controlled NAT fallback for legacy endpoints. Includes Terraform changes to networking modules, firewall rule updates, and verification steps.
- Non-goal: redesigning application-level policies or rewriting app egress rules. Not covering cross-region WAN optimizations.

Assumptions (call out environment variability):
- Clusters are in single VPC per customer; some have multiple private subnets.
- Private DNS currently uses conditional forwarders to an on-prem resolver. Some customers have host-based overrides (we discovered ~3 customers).
- Existing NAT instances are implemented either as cloud-managed NAT gateways or as egress VMs (customer-specific).
- We can change routing tables and firewall rules with a 2-minute outage window for control-plane calls; we must avoid any disruption for token-serving frontends.

High-level approach: staged rollout across tenants with three phases:
1) Canary (1 customer, low-QPS): deploy egress-proxy, enable passive monitoring, collect metrics, ensure no DNS regressions.
2) Progressive ramp (10 customers): enable active SNAT via proxy for test namespaces, monitor service-level metrics and network flows.
3) Full migration: flip default route for VPC to proxy, retire per-cluster NAT where safe.

Terraform changes (notes and snippets):
- New module: modules/egress-proxy-aws (or _gcp) to provision the proxy ASG, NLB, and route-table attachments. Module inputs: vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, allowed_dest_ranges, nat_fallback (bool), dns_forwarders.
- Plan to make minimal changes to existing modules: add an opt-in boolean to modules/vpc-egress to toggle proxy mode. This avoids refactoring all customer stacks at once.
- Important outputs: proxy_vip, proxy_security_group_id, route_table_association_id.

Terraform pseudo-snippet (for operator reference):
variable "egress_proxy_enabled" { default = false }
resource "aws_lb" "egress_nlb" {
  name               = "egress-nlb-${var.customer_id}"
  internal           = true
  load_balancer_type = "network"
  subnets            = var.private_subnet_ids
}

resource "aws_route" "to_egress_proxy" {
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.private.id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  network_interface_id   = aws_lb.egress_nlb.dns_name # placeholder, real implementation uses ENI target
  depends_on = [aws_lb.egress_nlb]
}

Operator checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] Confirm we have a current inventory of customer DNS overrides (Confluence: /page/priv-dns-inventory).
- [ ] Validate that proxy image version is signed and available in the private registry.
- [ ] Confirm security group rules: allow outbound 443/80 to allowed destinations; allow health checks from NLB subnets; deny raw 53/udp egress from proxies (we rely on forwarders).
- [ ] Prepare monitoring dashboards: egress-traffic, dns-failures, tcp-reset-rate, source-NAT-counts.
- [ ] Share planned maintenance windows with affected customer contacts (CS ticket created: JIRA-PRIV-1287).

Canary cutover steps (detailed):
1. Deploy egress-proxy module in customer's VPC in passive mode (no route changes). Verify pods come up and pass health checks.
2. Update security groups to allow NLB -> proxy traffic and proxy -> external (per allowed_dest_ranges).
3. Enable packet-capture/flow logs for the customer VPC for 24h baseline.
4. Configure pilot namespace: annotate workloads in a single test namespace to use proxy (via iptables sidecar or kube-router rule).
5. Verify DNS behavior: queries to private zones still resolve to internal IPs. Confirm no increase in NXDOMAIN or timeouts.
6. Run synthetic tests: curl to IMDS (should be blocked), curl to external endpoints, and TLS handshakes to common CDNs.
7. Observe metrics for 3 business days. If anomalies > threshold (5% error rate or 3x baseline latency), rollback to passive mode and file postmortem.

Progressive ramp notes and gating criteria:
- Gating metrics: 5xx rate on traffic through proxy < 0.3%, average egress latency increase < 15ms vs baseline, CPU/memory headroom > 30% on proxy nodes, no DNS resolution errors.
- Stagger customers by network topology class: small (<5 subnets), medium (5-15), large (>15) to mitigate blast radius.
- Schedule route flips during low-traffic windows for each customer and keep NAT fallback available for 48h.

Firewall and network policy changes:
- Update perimeter firewall rules to allow NLB VIPs as source for egress traffic (replace per-cluster NAT IP ranges).
- Kubernetes NetworkPolicies: add a lightweight egress policy that allows traffic only to proxy IPs by default; annotate namespaces to exempt legacy pods during ramp.
- Document required firewall rules for customer-managed edge: TCP:80/443 outbound from proxy VIP, ephemeral ports for NAT translations if needed, and deny direct 53 UDP from pods (force forwarding).

DNS considerations and migration steps:
- Preserve split-horizon behavior by preserving conditional forwarders on proxy nodes to the existing on‑prem resolvers.
- For customers with host overrides, create an exception list so those names bypass proxy forwarders and go to the legacy resolver. Flag these as "manual review required" in inventory.
- Investigate using DNS cache on proxy with TTL respect to reduce chattiness for common internal names.

Validation tests (automated and manual):
- Automated: k8s e2e job that deploys a test pod and runs an internal DNS resolution suite, external HTTP/TLS suite, and TTL compliance checks. Results should be stored in S3 with a customer-tagged folder.
- Manual: execute a sample of customer production flows (token health checks, model fetches) from test pods with traffic mirroring.
- Drift checks: Terraform plan must show only intended changes. Run a pre-cutover terraform plan and save artifact for audit.

Rollback plan (must be executable in <15 min):
- If high-severity failure occurs (application-level outages >5% or security incidents), revert route table to previous target (per-cluster NAT) using stored route table snapshot variables.
- Re-enable NAT gateway or re-point ASG target group back to NAT proxies.
- Revoke any temporary firewall rules added for the proxy VIPs.
- If DNS regressions occurred, rollback conditional forwarder changes first and block proxy DNS caching.

Telemetry and observability checklist to keep on during rollouts:
- Flow logs (VPC) + ENI metrics for NLB traffic.
- Per-tenant egress error counters and response latency histograms.
- DNS query success/failure rates, RTT percentiles.
- Proxy pod health (OOM, restarts) and kernel drop counters.
- Alerting thresholds pre-configured in Ops runbook: page on high error spike, page on DNS success <95% for 15m, page on proxy CPU >85% for 10m.

Open questions and TODOs (for triage meeting):
- Are there any customers using raw DNS over UDP from pods that must be supported? (Investigate recorded flow logs.)
- Should we include egress TLS SNI allowlist by default to reduce MITM-like failures?
- Implement a small alpha of transparent TLS passthrough before full migration to reduce certificate pinning issues.
- Determine retention for packet captures taken during canary (propose 7 days).

Post-migration cleanup checklist:
- [ ] Remove per-cluster NAT objects when stable for 14 days.
- [ ] Remove legacy route rules and update Terraform state to avoid orphan resources.
- [ ] Update runbooks and customer docs with new firewall IPs and expected behaviors.
- [ ] Run a retrospective and capture lessons learned in Confluence (linked_artifacts above).

Notes from experiments (quick log):
- Observed an edge case where tiny internal CNAME chains (>3) caused cached responses to lose internal IPs under a naive DNS cache. Fix: increase cache resolver logic to follow CNAMEs before caching.
- Proxy node became CPU-bound under TLS handshakes at 12k concurrent connections in stress test; horizontal pod autoscaler threshold adjusted and ASG min size increased by 1.

Appendix: Useful commands and artifacts
- terraform plan: cd infra/customers/${customer}/ && terraform plan -var 'egress_proxy_enabled=true'
- capture: aws ec2 create-flow-logs --resource-type ENI --resource-id eni-xxxxx --traffic-type ALL --log-group /aws/vpc/flow-logs
- kube: kubectl -n proxy get pods -o wide; kubectl logs -f deploy/egress-proxy
- verification script location: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-tools/egress-checks (branch: staged-egress)

End of runbook v0.2. This is a working document — please add findings and edits inline.
